deferredLuaNapiMutatorBindings.description: Indirect opcode -> N-API MUTATOR bindings via deferred Lua event handlers. Distinct from confirmedIndirectBindings (which pairs N-API READERS with opcode receiver per-actor field WRITES via a shared chain key). Here the binding shape is: opcode -> event-condition receiver -> queued event-condition object -> consumer drains the queue -> EventCondition vftable slot fires Lua handler -> handler calls N-API MUTATOR -> mutator targets global subsystem state (PlayerControl / LockonControl / TargetCursorControl lock counters) via the FUN_004D7580 singleton. The deferred-napi-writers pass trace establishes the 10-level call chain for each (luaHandler, opcode, napiMutator) tuple; the per-mutator vtable / override / wrapper / singleton-slot metadata is preserved so the binding survives Ghidra re-runs.
deferredLuaNapiMutatorBindings.schemaShapeNote: Each binding is keyed on (luaEventName, luaEventClass). writingOpcodes is the set of opcodes that, through their event-condition receivers, ultimately fire this Lua handler. napiMutators lists the mutator methods the Lua handler calls; for the 6 PlayerBase/MyPlayer lock methods the full C++ chain (stub VA, vtable slot, override, wrapper, singleton getter, singleton vtable slot) is recorded inline. uiSideMutators captures desktopWidget calls that touch UI-side subsystem state. guard is the Lua-side condition that gates whether the mutator fires (omitted when unconditional).
